title_en: E-Commerce Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is formulated for the purposes of protecting the lawful rights and interests of all parties in e-commerce, regulating e-commerce activities, maintaining market order, and promoting the sustained and healthy development of e-commerce.

Article 2 This Law shall apply to e-commerce activities within the territory of the People's Republic of China.
E-commerce as mentioned in this Law refers to business activities of selling goods or providing services through information networks such as the Internet.
Where laws or administrative regulations have provisions on the sale of goods or provision of services, such provisions shall apply. Financial products and services, and services that utilize information networks to provide content such as news information, audio and video programs, publications, and cultural products, shall not be subject to this Law.

Article 3 The State shall encourage the development of new forms of e-commerce, innovate business models, promote the research, development, and popularization of e-commerce technologies, advance the construction of the e-commerce credit system, create a market environment conducive to the innovative development of e-commerce, and give full play to the important role of e-commerce in promoting high-quality development, satisfying the people's ever-growing needs for a better life, and building an open economy.

Article 4 The State shall treat online and offline business activities equally, promote the integrated development of online and offline activities. People's governments at all levels and relevant departments shall not adopt discriminatory policies or measures, and shall not abuse administrative powers to exclude or restrict market competition.

Article 5 E-commerce operators, when engaging in business activities, shall follow the principles of voluntariness, equality, fairness, and good faith, abide by laws and commercial ethics, participate in market competition fairly, fulfill obligations in such aspects as consumer rights and interests protection, environmental protection, intellectual property protection, network security and personal information protection, bear responsibility for the quality of products and services, and accept supervision from the government and the public.

Article 6 The relevant departments of the State Council shall, according to their respective functions and duties, be responsible for work such as promoting the development of e-commerce and supervising and managing e-commerce. Local people's governments at or above the county level may, based on the actual conditions of their respective administrative regions, determine the division of departmental responsibilities for e-commerce within their administrative regions.

Article 7 The State shall establish a collaborative management system that conforms to the characteristics of e-commerce, and promote the formation of an e-commerce market governance system in which relevant departments, e-commerce industry organizations, e-commerce operators, consumers, and others participate.

Article 8 E-commerce industry organizations shall, in accordance with their charters, conduct industry self-discipline, establish and improve industry norms, promote the construction of industry integrity, and supervise and guide operators in this industry to participate in market competition fairly.

Article 9 For the purposes of this Law, e-commerce operators refer to natural persons, legal persons, and unincorporated organizations that engage in business activities of selling goods or providing services through information networks such as the Internet, including e-commerce platform operators, platform-based operators, and e-commerce operators that sell goods or provide services through self-built websites or other network services.
For the purposes of this Law, e-commerce platform operators refer to legal persons or unincorporated organizations that provide online business premises, transaction matching, information release and other services for two or more parties to a transaction in e-commerce, enabling such parties to independently conduct transaction activities.
For the purposes of this Law, platform-based operators refer to e-commerce operators that sell goods or provide services through e-commerce platforms.

Article 10 E-commerce operators shall register as market entities according to law, except for individuals who sell self-produced agricultural and sideline products or household handicraft products, individuals who use their skills to engage in convenience services for which no license is required according to law and sporadic small-value transactions, and other circumstances that do not require registration according to laws and administrative regulations.

Article 11 E-commerce operators shall perform tax obligations according to law and enjoy tax preferences according to law.
E-commerce operators that do not need to register as market entities in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article shall, after the occurrence of their first tax obligation, apply for tax registration in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations on tax collection administration and truthfully declare and pay taxes.

Article 12 Where an e-commerce operator needs to obtain relevant administrative licenses according to law to engage in business activities, it shall obtain the administrative licenses according to law.

Article 13 Goods sold or services provided by e-commerce operators shall meet the requirements for the protection of personal and property safety and environmental protection, and they shall not sell or provide goods or services whose transaction is prohibited by laws or administrative regulations.

Article 14 When selling goods or providing services, e-commerce operators shall issue paper invoices or electronic invoices and other purchase vouchers or service documents according to law. Electronic invoices and paper invoices have the same legal effect.

Article 15 E-commerce operators shall, in a prominent position on their homepages, continuously display their business license information, information on administrative licenses related to their business operations, and information indicating that they fall under the circumstances of not requiring market entity registration as specified in Article 10 of this Law, or links to the foregoing information.
If the information prescribed in the preceding paragraph changes, the e-commerce operator shall update the disclosed information in a timely manner.

Article 16 Where an e-commerce operator voluntarily terminates its e-commerce operations, it shall continuously display relevant information in a prominent position on its homepage for 30 days in advance.

Article 17 E-commerce operators shall comprehensively, truthfully, accurately, and promptly disclose information on goods or services to protect consumers' right to know and right of choice. E-commerce operators shall not engage in false or misleading commercial publicity, such as by fabricating transactions or creating user reviews, to deceive or mislead consumers.

Article 18 Where an e-commerce operator provides consumers with search results for goods or services based on their interests, hobbies, consumption habits, or other characteristics, it shall at the same time provide the consumers with options that are not tailored to their personal characteristics, respecting and protecting the legitimate rights and interests of consumers equally.
Where an e-commerce operator sends advertisements to consumers, it shall comply with the relevant provisions of the Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China.
Article 19 Where an e-commerce operator bundles goods or services, it shall draw consumers' attention in a prominent manner, and shall not make the bundled goods or services a default option.

Article 20 An e-commerce operator shall deliver goods or services to consumers in the manner and within the time limit as promised or agreed with consumers, and shall bear the risks and liabilities during the transportation of goods, except where the consumer separately chooses the courier service provider.

Article 21 Where an e-commerce operator collects deposits from consumers as agreed, it shall clearly state the method and procedure for refunding the deposit, and shall not set unreasonable conditions for the refund of the deposit. Where a consumer applies for a refund of the deposit and meets the conditions for refund, the e-commerce operator shall refund the deposit promptly.

Article 22 Where an e-commerce operator has a dominant market position due to factors such as its technological advantages, user numbers, control over related industries, and the dependence of other business operators on it in transactions, it shall not abuse its dominant market position to eliminate or restrict competition.

Article 23 When collecting and using users' personal information, e-commerce operators shall comply with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations on the protection of personal information.

Article 24 E-commerce operators shall clearly state the means and procedures for users to inquire, correct, or delete their information, and for users to cancel their accounts, and shall not set unreasonable conditions for the inquiry, correction, deletion of user information, or for the cancellation of user accounts.
Upon receiving a user's request to inquire, correct, or delete information, the e-commerce operator shall provide the inquiry or correct or delete the user's information in a timely manner after verifying the user's identity. Where a user cancels an account, the e-commerce operator shall immediately delete the user's information; where the information is retained in accordance with laws, administrative regulations, or the agreement between the parties, the information shall be retained accordingly.

Article 25 Where relevant competent authorities, in accordance with laws and administrative regulations, request an e-commerce operator to provide relevant e-commerce data and information, the e-commerce operator shall provide it. The relevant competent authorities shall take necessary measures to protect the security of the data and information provided by the e-commerce operator, and shall keep confidential the personal information, privacy, and trade secrets contained therein, and shall not disclose, sell, or illegally provide them to others.

Article 26 Where an e-commerce operator engages in cross-border e-commerce, it shall comply with the laws, administrative regulations, and relevant state provisions on import and export supervision and administration.

Article 27 An e-commerce platform operator shall require operators that apply to enter the platform to sell goods or provide services to submit true information on their identity, address, contact information, and administrative licenses, and shall verify, register, establish registration files, and regularly verify and update such information.
Where an e-commerce platform operator provides services to non-business users that enter the platform to sell goods or provide services, it shall comply with the relevant provisions of this Section.

Article 28 An e-commerce platform operator shall, in accordance with regulations, submit to the market regulatory authority the identity information of operators within the platform, remind operators that have not registered as market entities to register according to law, and cooperate with the market regulatory authority to facilitate registration for operators that should register as market entities, taking into account the characteristics of e-commerce.
An e-commerce platform operator shall, in accordance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations on tax collection administration, submit to the tax authority the identity information of operators within the platform and information related to tax payment, and shall remind e-commerce operators that do not need to register as market entities in accordance with Article 10 of this Law to handle tax registration in accordance with the provisions of Paragraph 2 of Article 11 of this Law.

Article 29 Where an e-commerce platform operator discovers that the information on commodities or services on its platform violates the provisions of Article 12 or Article 13 of this Law, it shall take necessary disposal measures according to law and report to the relevant competent authority.

Article 30 An e-commerce platform operator shall take technical measures and other necessary measures to ensure the security and stable operation of its network, prevent cyber crimes and illegal activities, effectively respond to cyber security incidents, and ensure the security of e-commerce transactions.
An e-commerce platform operator shall formulate an emergency response plan for cyber security incidents. When a cyber security incident occurs, it shall immediately activate the emergency response plan, take corresponding remedial measures, and report to the relevant competent authority.

Article 31 An e-commerce platform operator shall record and retain the information on commodities and services and the transaction information published on the platform, and shall ensure the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of such information. The retention period for the information on commodities and services and the transaction information shall be no less than three years from the date of completion of the transaction; where laws or administrative regulations provide otherwise, such provisions shall prevail.

Article 32 An e-commerce platform operator shall, following the principles of openness, fairness, and impartiality, formulate platform service agreements and transaction rules, specifying the rights and obligations regarding access to and withdrawal from the platform, guarantee of commodity and service quality, protection of consumers' rights and interests, and protection of personal information.

Article 33 An e-commerce platform operator shall continuously display on a prominent position on its homepage the platform service agreements and transaction rules or the link identifiers of the aforesaid information, and shall ensure that business operators and consumers can conveniently and completely view and download such information.

Article 34 Where an e-commerce platform operator revises the platform service agreements and transaction rules, it shall publicly solicit opinions on a prominent position on its homepage and take reasonable measures to ensure that relevant parties can express their opinions in a timely and full manner. The revised content shall be made public at least seven days before implementation.
Where a business operator on the platform does not accept the revised content and requests to withdraw from the platform, the e-commerce platform operator shall not obstruct such withdrawal and shall bear relevant liability in accordance with the service agreements and transaction rules before the revision.

Article 35 An e-commerce platform operator shall not, by using service agreements, transaction rules, technology, or other means, impose unreasonable restrictions or attach unreasonable conditions on the transactions, transaction prices, or transactions with other business operators of business operators on the platform, or charge unreasonable fees to business operators on the platform.

Article 36 Where an e-commerce platform operator, in accordance with the platform service agreements and transaction rules, imposes measures such as warnings, suspension, or termination of services on business operators on the platform for violating laws or regulations, it shall make a timely public announcement.

Article 37 Where an e-commerce platform operator conducts self-operated business on its platform, it shall clearly and conspicuously distinguish and mark the self-operated business from the business conducted by business operators on the platform, and shall not mislead consumers.
An e-commerce platform operator shall bear civil liability as a seller of commodities or a service provider according to law for the business it marks as self-operated.

Article 38 Where an e-commerce platform operator knows or should have known that the commodities sold or services provided by a business operator on the platform do not meet the requirements for the protection of personal and property safety, or there are other acts infringing upon the lawful rights and interests of consumers, and fails to take necessary measures, it shall bear joint and several liability with the business operator on the platform according to law.
With respect to commodities or services that concern the life and health of consumers, where an e-commerce platform operator fails to fulfill its duty of review over the qualifications of business operators on the platform, or fails to fulfill its duty of ensuring safety for consumers, causing damage to consumers, it shall bear corresponding liability according to law.

Article 39 An e-commerce platform operator shall establish and improve a credit evaluation system, make public the credit evaluation rules, and provide consumers with a means to evaluate the commodities sold or services provided on the platform.
An e-commerce platform operator shall not delete the evaluations made by consumers on the commodities sold or services provided on its platform.

Article 40 An e-commerce platform operator shall display the search results of commodities or services to consumers in multiple ways based on factors such as price, sales volume, and credit standing; for commodities or services ranked by bid, it shall prominently mark them as "advertisement".

Article 41 An e-commerce platform operator shall establish rules for the protection of intellectual property, strengthen cooperation with intellectual property rights holders, and protect intellectual property according to law.

Article 42 Where an intellectual property rights holder believes that its intellectual property has been infringed upon, it shall have the right to notify the e-commerce platform operator to take necessary measures such as deletion, blocking, disconnection of links, and termination of transactions and services. The notice shall include preliminary evidence of the infringement.
Upon receiving the notice, the e-commerce platform operator shall promptly take necessary measures and forward the notice to the business operator on the platform; if it fails to take necessary measures in a timely manner, it shall bear joint and several liability with the business operator on the platform for the expanded part of the damage.
Where damage is caused to a business operator on the platform due to an erroneous notice, the notifier shall bear civil liability according to law. Where an erroneous notice is sent maliciously, causing losses to the business operator on the platform, the notifier shall bear double compensation liability.

Article 43 Upon receiving the forwarded notice, a business operator on the platform may submit a declaration to the e-commerce platform operator stating that there is no infringement. The declaration shall include preliminary evidence of the absence of infringement.
Upon receiving the declaration, the e-commerce platform operator shall forward the declaration to the intellectual property rights holder who sent the notice and inform it that it may file a complaint with the relevant competent authority or initiate a lawsuit in the People's Court. If, within fifteen days after the declaration is forwarded to the intellectual property rights holder, the e-commerce platform operator does not receive a notice from the rights holder that it has filed a complaint or initiated a lawsuit, it shall promptly terminate the measures taken.
Article 44 An e-commerce platform operator shall make timely public announcements of the notices, declarations, and outcomes of handling received under Articles 42 and 43 of this Law.

Article 45 Where an e-commerce platform operator knows or should have known that a business operator on the platform is infringing upon intellectual property, it shall take necessary measures such as deletion, blocking, disconnection of links, and termination of transactions and services; if it fails to take necessary measures, it shall bear joint and several liability with the infringer.

Article 46 In addition to the services specified in Paragraph 2 of Article 9 of this Law, an e-commerce platform operator may, in accordance with the platform service agreements and transaction rules, provide services such as warehousing, logistics, payment and settlement, and delivery for e-commerce between business operators. An e-commerce platform operator providing services for e-commerce between business operators shall comply with laws, administrative regulations, and relevant state provisions, and shall not engage in transactions through centralized auction, market making, or other centralized trading methods, nor shall it engage in standardized contract transactions.

Article 47 The conclusion and performance of contracts by e-commerce parties shall be governed by the provisions of this Chapter and the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the Electronic Signature Law of the People's Republic of China, and other laws.

Article 48 The act of an e-commerce party using an automated information system to conclude or perform a contract shall have legal effect on the party using such system.
In e-commerce, a party shall be presumed to have the corresponding civil capacity for civil conduct. However, this shall not apply if there is evidence to the contrary sufficient to rebut such presumption.

Article 49 Where the information on goods or services published by an e-commerce operator meets the conditions for an offer, a contract shall be formed when a user selects such goods or services and successfully submits the order. If the parties have otherwise agreed, such agreement shall prevail.
An e-commerce operator shall not agree in standard terms or by other means that the contract is not formed after the consumer has paid the price; if standard terms or the like contain such content, such content shall be null and void.

Article 50 An e-commerce operator shall clearly, comprehensively, and explicitly inform users of the steps for concluding a contract, matters needing attention, methods for downloading, and other matters, and shall ensure that users can conveniently and completely read and download such information.
An e-commerce operator shall ensure that users can correct input errors before submitting an order.

Article 51 Where the subject matter of a contract is the delivery of goods and such goods are delivered by express logistics, the time of delivery shall be the time when the consignee signs for the goods. Where the subject matter of a contract is the provision of services, the time of delivery shall be the time indicated in the electronic or physical certificate generated; if the aforementioned certificate does not indicate a time or the indicated time is inconsistent with the actual time of service provision, the time of actual service provision shall be the time of delivery.
Where the subject matter of a contract is delivered by online transmission, the time of delivery shall be the time when the subject matter enters the specific system designated by the other party and becomes retrievable and identifiable.
If the parties to the contract have otherwise agreed on the method and time of delivery, such agreement shall prevail.

Article 52 E-commerce parties may agree to deliver goods by express logistics.
An express logistics service provider, when providing express logistics services for e-commerce, shall abide by laws and administrative regulations and shall comply with the committed service specifications and time limits. When delivering goods, the express logistics service provider shall remind the consignee to inspect the goods in person; if delivery is to be made to another person on behalf of the consignee, the consent of the consignee shall be obtained.
An express logistics service provider shall use environmentally friendly packaging materials in accordance with regulations to achieve reduction and reuse of packaging materials.
An express logistics service provider may, while providing express logistics services, accept the entrustment of an e-commerce operator to provide cash-on-delivery services.

Article 53 E-commerce parties may agree to pay the price by electronic payment.
An electronic payment service provider, when providing electronic payment services for e-commerce, shall comply with state regulations, inform users of the functions, usage methods, matters needing attention, related risks, fee standards, and other matters of the electronic payment service, and shall not impose unreasonable transaction conditions. The electronic payment service provider shall ensure the integrity, consistency, traceability, and non-tamperability of electronic payment instructions.
An electronic payment service provider shall provide to users free of charge reconciliation services and transaction records for the most recent three years.

Article 54 Where an electronic payment service provider provides electronic payment services that do not comply with the state requirements for payment security management, causing losses to users, it shall bear compensation liability.

Article 55 Before issuing a payment instruction, a user shall verify the complete information included in the payment instruction, such as the amount and the payee.
If a payment instruction is erroneous, the electronic payment service provider shall promptly identify the cause and take relevant measures to correct it. If losses are caused to the user, the electronic payment service provider shall bear compensation liability, unless it can prove that the payment error was not caused by its own reasons.

Article 56 After completing an electronic payment, the electronic payment service provider shall promptly and accurately provide the user with information confirming the payment in a manner consistent with the agreement.

Article 57 A user shall properly keep security tools such as transaction passwords and electronic signature data. If a user discovers that a security tool is lost, stolen, or used for unauthorized payment, the user shall promptly notify the electronic payment service provider.
Losses caused by unauthorized payment shall be borne by the electronic payment service provider; if the electronic payment service provider can prove that the unauthorized payment was caused by the user's fault, it shall not bear liability.
When an electronic payment service provider discovers that a payment instruction is unauthorized, or receives a notice from the user that a payment instruction is unauthorized, it shall immediately take measures to prevent the expansion of losses. If the electronic payment service provider fails to take timely measures, causing the expansion of losses, it shall bear liability for the expanded portion of the losses.

Article 58 The State shall encourage e-commerce platform operators to establish a mechanism for guaranteeing the quality of goods and services that is conducive to the development of e-commerce and the protection of consumers' rights and interests.
Where an e-commerce platform operator and an operator on the platform agree to establish a consumer rights and interests guarantee deposit, both parties shall make clear agreements on the amount of the deposit to be drawn, management, use, and refund methods.
Where a consumer requests the e-commerce platform operator to bear advance compensation liability, and the subsequent recourse by the e-commerce platform operator against the operator on the platform after compensation, the relevant provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests shall apply.

Article 59 An e-commerce business operator shall establish a convenient and effective complaint and report mechanism, disclose the methods of complaint and report and other information, and promptly accept and handle complaints and reports.

Article 60 E-commerce disputes may be resolved through negotiation and settlement, requesting mediation by consumer organizations, industry associations, or other mediation organizations established according to law, filing complaints with relevant authorities, applying for arbitration, or instituting prosecution, among other means.

Article 61 Where a consumer purchases goods or receives services on an e-commerce platform and a dispute arises with an operator on the platform, the e-commerce platform operator shall actively assist the consumer in safeguarding the consumer's lawful rights and interests.

Article 62 In the handling of e-commerce disputes, an e-commerce business operator shall provide original contracts and transaction records. Where, because the e-commerce business operator loses, forges, alters, destroys, conceals, or refuses to provide the aforesaid materials, which results in the People's Court, arbitration institution, or relevant authorities being unable to ascertain the facts, the e-commerce business operator shall bear corresponding legal liability.

Article 63 An e-commerce platform operator may establish an online dispute resolution mechanism, formulate and publicize dispute resolution rules, and resolve disputes between the parties fairly and justly on the basis of the principle of voluntariness.

Article 64 The State Council and the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall incorporate the development of e-commerce into the national economic and social development plans, formulate scientific and reasonable industrial policies, and promote the innovative development of e-commerce.

Article 65 The State Council and the local people's governments at or above the county level and their relevant departments shall take measures to support and promote green packaging, warehousing, and transportation, and promote the green development of e-commerce.

Article 66 The State shall promote the construction of e-commerce infrastructure and logistics networks, improve the e-commerce statistical system, and strengthen the development of the e-commerce standards system.
Article 67 The State shall promote the application of e-commerce in various fields of the national economy and support the integrated development of e-commerce with various industries.

Article 68 The State shall promote the application of Internet technologies in agricultural production, processing, circulation, and other links, encourage all types of social resources to strengthen cooperation, promote the development of rural e-commerce, and give play to the role of e-commerce in targeted poverty alleviation.

Article 69 The State shall maintain the security of e-commerce transactions, protect the information of e-commerce users, encourage the development and application of e-commerce data, and ensure the orderly and free flow of e-commerce data in accordance with law.
The State shall take measures to promote the establishment of a public data sharing mechanism and encourage e-commerce business operators to use public data in accordance with law.

Article 70 The State shall support credit evaluation institutions established in accordance with law in carrying out e-commerce credit evaluation and providing e-commerce credit evaluation services to the public.

Article 71 The State shall promote the development of cross-border e-commerce, establish and improve customs, taxation, import and export inspection and quarantine, payment and settlement, and other management systems that suit the characteristics of cross-border e-commerce, improve the level of facilitation in all aspects of cross-border e-commerce, and support cross-border e-commerce platform operators and others in providing warehousing and logistics, customs declaration, inspection declaration, and other services for cross-border e-commerce.
The State shall support small and micro enterprises in engaging in cross-border e-commerce.

Article 72 The national import and export administrative departments shall advance the construction of a comprehensive service and supervision system for customs declaration, tax payment, inspection and quarantine, and other aspects of cross-border e-commerce, optimize supervision procedures, promote the realization of information sharing, mutual recognition of supervision, and mutual assistance in law enforcement, and improve the efficiency of services and supervision of cross-border e-commerce. Cross-border e-commerce business operators may use electronic documents to handle relevant procedures with the national import and export administrative departments.

Article 73 The State shall promote the establishment of exchanges and cooperation on cross-border e-commerce with different countries and regions, participate in the formulation of international rules on e-commerce, and promote international mutual recognition of electronic signatures, electronic identities, and others.
The State shall promote the establishment of cross-border e-commerce dispute resolution mechanisms with different countries and regions.

Article 74 An e-commerce business operator that sells goods or provides services, fails to perform its contractual obligations or performs its contractual obligations not in conformity with the agreement, or causes damage to others, shall bear civil liability according to law.

Article 75 An e-commerce business operator that violates the provisions of Articles 12 and 13 of this Law by engaging in business activities without obtaining the relevant administrative license, or selling or providing goods or services the transaction of which is prohibited by laws or administrative regulations, or failing to perform the obligation to provide information as prescribed in Article 25 of this Law, or an e-commerce platform operator that violates the provisions of Article 46 of this Law by engaging in transactions through centralized trading or by trading standardized contracts, shall be punished in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations.

Article 77 An e-commerce business operator that provides search results in violation of the provisions of paragraph 1 of Article 18 of this Law, or ties in the sale of goods or services in violation of the provisions of Article 19 of this Law, shall be ordered by the market regulatory department to make corrections within a specified period, and its illegal gains shall be confiscated, and it may also be fined not less than 50,000 yuan and not more than 200,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, it shall also be fined not less than 200,000 yuan and not more than 500,000 yuan.

Article 78 An e-commerce business operator that violates the provisions of Article 21 of this Law by failing to clearly indicate to consumers the methods and procedures for refunding deposits, setting unreasonable conditions for refunding deposits, or failing to refund deposits in a timely manner, shall be ordered by the relevant competent authority to make corrections within a specified period, and may be fined not less than 50,000 yuan and not more than 200,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, it shall be fined not less than 200,000 yuan and not more than 500,000 yuan.

Article 79 Where an e-commerce operator violates the provisions of laws and administrative regulations on the protection of personal information, or fails to perform the cybersecurity guarantee obligations prescribed in Article 30 of this Law and relevant laws and administrative regulations, it shall be penalized in accordance with the provisions of the Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China and other laws and administrative regulations.

Article 82 Where an e-commerce platform operator violates Article 35 of this Law by imposing unreasonable restrictions or additional unreasonable conditions on transactions, transaction prices, or transactions with other operators of businesses on the platform, or by charging unreasonable fees to businesses on the platform, the market regulatory department shall order it to rectify within a time limit and may impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, it shall be fined not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 2,000,000 yuan.

Article 83 Where an e-commerce platform operator violates Article 38 of this Law by failing to take necessary measures against acts of businesses on the platform that infringe upon consumers' legitimate rights and interests, or by failing to fulfill the obligation of examining the qualifications of businesses on the platform, or by failing to fulfill the safety guarantee obligation to consumers, the market regulatory department shall order it to rectify within a time limit and may impose a fine of not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, it shall be ordered to suspend operations for rectification and shall also be fined not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 2,000,000 yuan.

Article 84 Where an e-commerce platform operator violates Articles 42 and 45 of this Law by failing to take necessary measures according to law against acts of infringement of intellectual property rights by businesses on the platform, the relevant intellectual property administrative department shall order it to rectify within a time limit; if it fails to rectify within the time limit, it shall be fined not less than 50,000 yuan but not more than 500,000 yuan; if the circumstances are serious, it shall be fined not less than 500,000 yuan but not more than 2,000,000 yuan.

Article 85 Where an e-commerce operator violates the provisions of this Law by selling goods or providing services that do not meet the requirements for ensuring personal and property safety, engaging in unfair competition practices such as false or misleading commercial publicity, abusing its dominant market position, or engaging in acts such as infringing upon intellectual property rights or consumers' rights and interests, it shall be penalized in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws.

Article 86 Where an e-commerce operator commits an illegal act prescribed in this Law, it shall be recorded in the credit file in accordance with the provisions of relevant laws and administrative regulations, and shall be publicized.

Article 87 Where a staff member of a department legally responsible for e-commerce supervision and administration neglects their duties, abuses their powers, or engages in malpractices for personal gain, or divulges, sells, or illegally provides to others the personal information, privacy, or trade secrets known to them in the course of performing their duties, legal liability shall be investigated according to law.

Article 88 Where a violation of the provisions of this Law constitutes a violation of public security administration, a public security administration penalty shall be imposed according to law; if the act constitutes a crime, criminal liability shall be investigated according to law.
Article 89 This Law shall come into force as of January 1, 2019.
